children.text: History is the study, analysis and interpretation of the past based on surviving artifacts. Film is a visual representation of moving pictures with sound. Film and history interconnect, as film acts as a mechanical reproduction of history relaying the historical past to please a larger audience. It also acts as a way to narrate historical events and the atmosphere of the time period as a visual mechanism for audiences.

Historical fiction film involves the dramatisation of historical events and individuals (who may be fictional) in order to draw viewer engagement. In such films it is evident that these films are not historically accurate, but the audiences are able to get a glimpse of the past through characters, customs, time period, speech, dialogue, conflict and many more. Storytelling in historical films creates a balance between historical events and real modern-life dilemmas.

An example of a historical fiction film is ‘Marie Antoinette’ (2006) directed by Sofia Coppola. This film is a dramatised depiction of Marie Antoinette’s life at the Palace of Versailles, marriage to King Louis XVI and the uprising of the French Resolution. Sofia Coppola uses an alternative method of visualising the life of Marie Antoinette by using anachronisms that include the use of punk-pop songs for example the shopping montage utilised the song ‘I Want Candy’ by punk-pop Bow Wow Wow and incorporating contemporary items such as the Converse sneakers to give the audience the perspective of a teenage girl.

This film is centric in its customising and design, and in the film Coppola strikes a balance between 18th Century historical dressing with a modern flair. Custom design in film is significant as a character’s story is visualised through their clothing. In the film, costuming was able to represent the atmosphere of 18th century France, to set a certain mood, and to project the state of mind of Marie Antoinette. A scene in the film, the shopping sequence, with the song ‘I Want Candy as the sound of the scene indicates the accurate luxurious nature of Marie Antoinette and her lavish spending but it is also a cross reference to today’s fashion and youth culture and the film’s main object is the perspective of teenagers and not strictly in the 18th century period piece.
